title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming

headline_result.text: Given only weights and a natural-language instruction (no data, forward passes or gradients), GPT-6 Astra implanted a trigger backdoor with 100% post-edit attack success on an MNIST MLP (6 changed parameters, clean accuracy unchanged), ResNet-18 (clean accuracy -1.43 points) and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (0.02% of weights); all five LLM editors succeeded on the MLP, four on ResNet-18, and only Astra on Qwen.

notes_for_review: First security study of WSP: it shows that a frontier LLM, given weights and an instruction but no data or forward passes, can return a backdoored model with high attack success and small clean-accuracy loss, outperforming data-poisoning fine-tuning on edit size. Evidence is thin on repetition: one returned model per editor-target pair, no record of failed or refused attempts, no random-edit control, and no released code. Vision editors were allowed to consult public reference material, and cross-editor differences may partly reflect access or harness rather than capability.
